description.narrative: Det långsiktiga målet med insatsen är att säkerställa att kvinnor och unga kan delta på lika villkor i samhället och kan utöva sin rätt att bestämma om, när och hur många barn de ska skaffa; ha rätt till information och tjänster av hög kvalitet relaterat till sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter (SRHR), samt rätt att leva fria från våld och tvång. Syftet med projektet är att ge kvinnor och unga människor möjlighet att utöva SRHR, särskilt 1) sin rätt till högkvalitativ och lyhörd SRHR- och GBV-information och tjänster, 2) sin rätt till jämställt och socialt inkluderande deltagande i beslutsfattande i deras samhällen, och 3) deras rätt att leva ett liv fritt från alla typer av GBV.

The long­term goal of this contribution is to ensure that women and young people participate equally in society and can exercise their right to decide if, when, and how many children to have; right to SRHR­related information and high­quality services; and right to be free from violence and coercion. The aim of the project is to empower women and young people to exercise their SRHR, specifically 1) their right to high­quality and responsive SRHR and GBV information and services, 2) their right to gender­ equitable and socially inclusive participation in decision­ making spaces in their communities, and 3) their right to live a life free from all types of GBV.

The overall objectives of the Project are 1)Increasing rightsholders (young people and women´s) capacity to know, claim and realize their rights, individually and collectively, for equitable gender norms and SRH. 2)Strengthening systems and duty bearers to deliver high-quality, gender- and youth responsive and socially inclusive SRHR information and services. 3)Bolstering existing accountability mechanisms and advocacy efforts to garner support and ownership over fulfilling SRHR. 4)Strengthening linkages with other rights-based and positive youth development and women´s empowerment initiatives.

EXAMPLES PER OBJECTIVE 1. Increasing rights holders (young people and womens) capacity.... Digital Advocacy: A youthled campaign using social media (Telegram, Instagram, LinkedIn) shared SRHR information, reaching 371 youth directly and over 12,000 women and outofschool youth via Yetena Wegs platforms. Male Engagement: The Men As Partners module was adapted to the local context to promote gendersensitive discussions among men through schools and community sessions. Youth Participation: A Youth Advisory Council of 60 members (including 41 females and 7 with disabilities) led awareness activities, panel discussions, and donations. Members received training in SRHR, life skills, leadership, and advocacy, supported by mentorship.
2. Strengthening systems and duty bearers to deliver highquality,gender and youthresponsive and socially inclusive SRHR information and services. EngenderHealth provided technical assistance to national and regional government partners across health, justice, education, and social sectors. For example by supporting development of GBV case management manual and male survivor care, including training at a referral hospital. Further, they contributed to revision of the national youth policy and development of womens empowerment guides. They also facilitated learning visits to onestop centers for senior government officials helped create standards and compliance tools for onestop centers integrated gender and youthsensitive tools into Ministry of Health training materials.
3. Bolstering existing accountability mechanisms and advocacy efforts... EngenderHealth built strategic alliances with youth and womenled organizations and professional associations to counter antichoice movements and promote SRHR and safe abortion care (SAC).Through digital campaigns and webinars, the project trained 167 young healthcare professionals and reached 251 medical students, enhancing their knowledge and values around SAC.The project supported four professional conferences, strengthened media partnerships, and contributed to national advocacy platforms, including Coalition for Comprehensive Abortion Care (CoCAC), to influence policy and public discourse on SRHR and GBV.
4. Strengthening linkages with other rightsbased and positive youth development and womens empowerment initiatives. Strategic partnerships with EWDO and Mella have strengthened grassroots advocacy for SRHR and GBV, with 60 community volunteers mobilized and organizational capacity enhanced to influence policy and decisionmaking. National events like International Womens Day and World Contraception Day successfully elevated public discourse on disability inclusion, womens rights, and access to quality family planning, engaging over 330 stakeholders including lawmakers and civil society leaders. Media engagement during the 16 Days of Activism led to improved awareness and reporting standards on SRHR and GBV among 39 trained journalists, resulting in broader, more inclusive media coverage through collaborations with national outlets like Fana Broadcasting.
